extracted.intended_audience: instructional designers, educators, and course developers creating online learning materials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for designing effective online learning materials based on behaviorist, cognitivist, constructivist, and connectivist theories; intended to inform instructional strategy, media use, assessment, and learner support in online courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner-centered design and adequate support
rubrics_metrics.description: Online learning materials must be designed properly, with the learners and learning in focus, and adequate support must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doing it right means designing with learners and learning as the focus and providing appropriate support resources; updated materials should be accessible immediately and systems should help determine learners' needs and expertise to assign appropriate materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity, interactivity, and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Online learning should have high authenticity (learning in workplace context), high interactivity, and high collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities that situate learning in real contexts, enable interaction with content/peers/instructors, and foster collaborative work to enhance relevance and transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize instructional strategy over technology as the driver of learning
rubrics_metrics.description: The instructional strategy, not the technology, primarily influences the quality of learning; technologies are vehicles that deliver instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and design pedagogical approaches that promote meaningful learning, linking new information to prior knowledge, encouraging metacognition, and tailoring strategies to outcomes rather than assuming the medium itself will produce learning gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate multiple learning theories and apply connectivism where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no single learning theory for online learning; designers should use a combination of behaviorist, cognitivist, constructivist principles and incorporate connectivist ideas for networked/distributed learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt established theories for digital contexts, integrate principles (e.g., sequencing, scaffolding, reflection, social learning), and use connectivist principles to support learning in rapidly changing, networked information environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: State explicit learning outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners should be told the explicit outcomes of the learning so they can set expectations and judge whether they have achieved the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state lesson/course outcomes at the outset to guide learner attention and self-assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate assessment to check achievement and provide corrective feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners must be tested to determine whether they have achieved the learning outcomes; online testing and other assessments should be integrated into the learning sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include formative and summative assessments that diagnose learner understanding and provide timely feedback so learners can take corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence learning materials appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning materials must be sequenced to promote learning (e.g., simple to complex, known to unknown, knowledge to application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design progression that scaffolds skills and knowledge; consider competency-based approaches and clear prerequisite structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide timely and informative feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners must be provided with feedback so they can monitor how they are doing and take corrective action if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement feedback mechanisms throughout lessons (automated, peer, instructor) tied to assessments and activities to support mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use perceptual/design strategies to capture attention and support working memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies should allow learners to perceive and attend to information so it can be transferred to working memory (e.g., placement, attributes of screen, pacing, mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place important information centrally, highlight critical elements (headings, formatting), tell learners why they should take the lesson, match difficulty to learner cognitive level, and avoid non-essential sensations that overload attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activate and build on existing cognitive structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Design should enable learners to retrieve existing information from long-term memory to make sense of new information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advance organizers (comparative or expository), conceptual models, pre-instructional questions, and prerequisite tests to activate prior knowledge and set expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chunk information to avoid working memory overload
rubrics_metrics.description: Information should be organized into manageable chunks (Miller's 7±2), presenting between five and nine items per screen and using information maps for structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide generalized overview maps (linear, hierarchical, spider-shaped), break down items into sub-items, and show the overall map again with relationships illustrated at lesson end; encourage learners to generate maps for deeper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote deep processing through higher-order tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use strategies that require application, analysis, synthesis, and evaluation to facilitate transfer into long-term memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include real-life applications, problem-solving tasks, projects and activities that encourage deep cognitive engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodate individual differences and learning styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a variety of learning strategies to cater to different learning styles (e.g., Kolb LSI, Myers-Briggs distinctions) and cognitive styles (field-dependent vs. field-independent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide multiple activity types so learners can select those matching their preferences (concrete examples, reflection, theory work, active experimentation); tailor instructor presence and support based on learner style (e.g., assimilators prefer high instructor presence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present information in multiple modes (dual coding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information should be presented in different modes (textual, verbal, visual) to encourage encoding and transfer to long-term memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible combine text with graphics, audio, animations or video to leverage dual-coding benefits and support diverse processing preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use motivation strategies (ARCS: Attention, Relevance, Confidence, Satisfaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners should be motivated using intrinsic and extrinsic strategies; Keller's ARCS model should guide motivational design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention: capture and maintain attention with an engaging start and activities. Relevance: explain importance and real-life benefits. Confidence: design for success, set expectations, sequence appropriately. Satisfaction: provide feedback and opportunities to apply learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage metacognition and reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners should be given opportunities to use metacognitive skills to monitor and adjust their learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed self-check questions, reflective exercises, and feedback throughout lessons; encourage learning journals and guided reflection to support self-regulated learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for transfer to real-life situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Online strategies should facilitate transfer by using simulations, real-life cases, assignments and projects that apply knowledge in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include authentic tasks and opportunities to apply learning across contexts to support meaningful learning and contextualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make learning active and student-driven
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning should be an active process with learners engaged in meaningful activities that promote high-level processing and personal meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor activities that require learners to apply information practically, make decisions, and take initiative rather than passive reception of content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support knowledge construction rather than passive reception
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners should construct their own knowledge with the instructor as advisor and facilitator, not sole knowledge source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide interactive instruction that allows students to experience information first-hand, contextualize it, and personalize their learning agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage collaborative and cooperative learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative and cooperative activities should be used to facilitate constructivist learning and social presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design group work that leverages members' expertise and learning styles; structure membership so individuals benefit from peers' strengths and provide real-life experience of teamwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give learners control with guided discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners should be given control of the learning process through guided discovery, making decisions about learning goals with instructor guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance learner autonomy with scaffolding to ensure productive exploration and goal-directed learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time and mechanisms for reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners should be given time and opportunities to reflect and internalize information (e.g., embedded questions, learning journals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reflection prompts during lessons and require or encourage reflective summaries or journals to support transformative and meaningful learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure meaningfulness through relevant examples and choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning materials should include examples that relate to learners and assignments that allow choice of meaningful activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize content with learner-relevant examples and design projects that permit personalization and real-world relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for interactivity and social presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning should be interactive to promote higher-level learning, social presence, and development of personal meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use discussion, feedback, group activities, and tools that enhance interaction between learners and instructors to build social presence and support deep engagement.
